senses.label: Lending at interest
senses.summary: Money is lent at interest; debt and default are matters of law and honour.
markers: interest is a private charge owed to the lender
hazards: 'Usury' is not a modern word here: Latin usura is ordinary interest.

sources.citation: Aristophanes, Clouds (first produced 423 BCE; surviving text revised c. 420–417)
sources.note: Strepsiades' debts and the interest on them, due monthly at the 'Old and New' day, are the play's premise.
The Roman refinement: Cicero's edict in Cilicia caps interest at one per cent a month.

senses.label: Usury as sin
senses.summary: Taking interest is morally wrong, at first for clergy and later for all Christians.
markers: lending at interest is a sin

sources.note: Clergy forbidden to lend at interest.

senses.label: Central banking and policy rates
senses.summary: A central bank sets the price of money for a whole economy, raising or lowering rates to steer it.
markers: a national bank sets interest rates to steer the economy

sources.note: Later the model of central banking.
